name: Effy AI
what: Effy AI is a self-serve 360 feedback and performance review tool. It is made by Effy AI OU, a company registered in Tallinn, Estonia. Effy also sells goals and OKRs, one-on-ones and probation reviews.
summary: Effy sells 360° Reviews as a standalone plan at $3 per seat per month, billed annually, so 50 employees cost $1,800 a year. Teams of up to 5 users can use it free. Effy says it runs on AWS and offers an EU region, but its security page names no region and its DPA allows processing worldwide. AI writes the review forms and summarises the feedback, and Effy states that it does not use customer data to train AI models.

ai: Yes: AI forms, summaries, bias checks
certs: None. ISO 27001 and SOC 2 planned for 2027

The DPA says Effy may process personal data on a global basis and does not commit to a location. The privacy notice says data may be processed in the United States.

The list price is public: $3 per seat per month, billed annually, with no minimum and no implementation fee.
Anonymity is set per review type, so peer feedback can be anonymous while manager ratings stay visible.
AI writes review forms, summarises comments and checks written feedback for bias.
Slack requests and reminders, and sign-in with Google, Microsoft or Slack.
PDF and CSV export, heatmaps and 9-box grids.
limitations: No minimum number of responses before scores show is published.
No security certificate. ISO 27001 and SOC 2 are planned for 2027.
The security page (3 October 2024) gives two different statements on encryption at rest.
Supported languages, a Microsoft Teams integration and HRIS connectors are not listed.
AI model providers are not named, and the subprocessor list did not display.
fit: Small teams that want AI-written forms and summaries, including teams of 5 people or fewer.

faq.q: How much does Effy AI cost for 50 employees?
faq.a: $1,800 a year: $3 per seat per month × 50 seats × 12 months, billed annually. This is the 360° Reviews plan with one review per user per year. The price for multiple reviews per user per year is $6 per seat per month, which is $3,600 a year for 50 seats.

faq.q: Is Effy AI 360 feedback anonymous?
faq.a: It depends on the setting. Effy lets you set anonymity per review type, for example anonymous peer feedback with visible manager ratings. Effy does not publish a minimum number of responses before scores show. Its 360 page says anonymity can break in small teams.

faq.q: Where does Effy AI store data?
faq.a: Effy says it hosts on Amazon Web Services and that an EU region is available. Its security page names no region. Its DPA allows processing on a global basis, and its privacy notice says data may be processed in the United States. The company is registered in Estonia.

faq.q: Does Effy AI use AI on feedback?
faq.a: Yes. Effy uses AI to write review forms, summarise comments per person and per cycle, and check written feedback for bias. The privacy notice states that Effy does not use customer data to train AI or machine-learning models. Effy does not publish which AI model providers it uses.

faq.q: Is Effy AI free?
faq.a: Yes, for up to 5 users. The free plan has full access to 360 reviews, needs no credit card and has no time limit. Larger teams pay from $3 per seat per month.

name: Spidergap
what: Spidergap is a 360 feedback tool made by Bridging Insight Ltd, which gives a London, UK address. Spidergap sells 360 feedback only.
summary: Spidergap sells 360 feedback as a standalone product, priced per person who receives feedback. 50 people cost €4,559 a year on the Pro plan (€4,659 on Starter). Data is stored on servers in the UK and the European Economic Area, and the company holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. No AI feature appears on the vendor's pages.

eu: Yes, servers in the UK and EEA

features.raters: Self-assessment, plus feedback providers in role groups. The help centre names managers or coaches, senior colleagues, peers, direct reports, customers and suppliers as examples. Reports can combine groups.
features.nomination: The administrator picks the feedback providers, or the person being assessed picks them through a personal link with no login. When people pick their own, an approver (for example the line manager or coach) can review and change the list before invitations go out. Self-enrolment is a Pro feature.
features.anonymity: Admins set this per role group. By default, a group with fewer than 3 responses is combined with other groups, for example into a group called Others. Multiple-choice and text answers have separate settings. Admins can raise the threshold to 4 or 5. They can also set a group to always show answers, or to show each text answer with the name of the person who gave it. Self-assessment cannot be anonymised. The help centre says manager and coach feedback generally needs no anonymising, and warns that writing style can still identify a person who wrote a text answer.
features.questions: A preset questionnaire template. The vendor states it was validated with over 100 behavioural psychologists, HR directors, managers and employees. The questionnaire is fully customisable. A competency library: Not found.
features.reports: A PDF report per person, shared by the administrator. Admins can hide or show report pages (Pro). The help centre describes group results export to PowerPoint or Word, raw data export to Excel, and comparison against industry norms. Details of the report layout: see the vendor's sample report.
features.languages: The pricing page says Starter can translate into 100+ languages. The help centre says translation is manual, covers the questionnaire, emails and report, and allows one language per project. It lists 28 languages, including Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Italian, and says others may work. Right-to-left languages such as Arabic are not supported.
features.integrations: SSO on the Pro and Enterprise plans. No customer API: the help centre says Spidergap has a private API that only its own team can use. A help centre topic covers HR system integration. Slack and Microsoft Teams: Not found.
features.ai: None found. No AI feature or AI provider appears on the pricing, security, privacy or subprocessor pages.

security.hosting: The privacy policy says servers are in the UK and the European Economic Area. The security page says Europe. Google manages the servers, and Rackspace is also named. Spidergap says it will tell users before it changes the hosting location. Region choice: Not published.
security.certificates: ISO/IEC 27001:2022. The certificate is issued to Bridging Insight Ltd. Spidergap says it is recertified every 3 years with annual surveillance audits. The page gives no certification body or dates. Google and Rackspace hold SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 reports. Spidergap names no SOC report of its own. External penetration tests run at least once a year. The security page was last updated on 20 June 2024.
security.ai_subprocessors: No AI provider is listed. The subprocessor list (updated 27 October 2023) names Google Ireland, Rackspace US, Intercom, HubSpot, The Rocket Science Group, ActiveCampaign Postmark, Dropbox International, Skype, Zoom and Slack.
security.gdpr: Spidergap is the controller of account data and the processor of data that customers collect about other people. A DPA can be signed (the help centre has an article on it). Soft-deleted data is deleted permanently within 30 to 60 days, and backups are kept for about 12 months. Customers can ask for their whole account to be deleted. Staff outside the EEA may access data under standard contractual clauses. EU representative: Not found.

strengths: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, with data on servers in the UK and the European Economic Area.
The price per person reviewed is public in GBP, EUR and USD. Admins and raters are free.
The first 360 assessment is free to run.
People can pick their own raters, with an optional approver.
Anonymity thresholds are documented: groups under 3 responses are combined by default, and admins can raise the threshold.
The questionnaire, emails and report can be translated into 28 documented languages.
limitations: The cost grows with each person reviewed: 50 people cost €4,559 a year at the lowest list price.
No customer API. SSO needs the Pro or Enterprise plan.
The pricing page says 100+ languages. The help centre lists 28, uses manual translation and does not support right-to-left languages.
The security page was last updated on 20 June 2024 and the subprocessor list on 27 October 2023.
fit: Organisations, coaches and consultants that run 360 rounds for named people and need ISO/IEC 27001 and European hosting.

faq.q: How much does Spidergap cost for 50 employees?
faq.a: €4,559 a year on the Pro plan: €2,199 for the first 10 people plus 40 more at €59. Starter costs €4,659 for the same 50 people (€1,099 plus 40 at €89). These are annual list prices. Enterprise is quote only.

faq.q: Is Spidergap 360 feedback anonymous?
faq.a: Yes, by setting. By default, a rater group with fewer than 3 responses is combined with other groups, for multiple-choice and text answers separately. Admins can raise the threshold, show a group's answers without combining them, or show each text answer with the giver's name. Self-assessment cannot be anonymised.

faq.q: Where does Spidergap store data?
faq.a: On servers in the UK and the European Economic Area, managed by Google. The security page also names Rackspace. Spidergap says it will tell users before it changes the hosting location. A choice of region is not published.

faq.q: Does Spidergap use AI on feedback?
faq.a: None found. Spidergap's pricing, security, privacy and subprocessor pages mention no AI feature and list no AI provider.

faq.q: Does Spidergap have a free trial?
faq.a: Yes. You can run one 360 assessment free, with all Starter functions. There is no free plan.

The report-filtering guide says its filters always exclude the Self group and any group marked as a manager group.
features.questions: A competency library of 80+ competencies. Teams can import their own competencies and write custom questions. AI survey generation builds a survey from a role description (Essentials and above). Surveys can mix rating scales, open questions and multiple choice.
features.reports: Individual, group and change-over-time reports. Essentials has 5 standard report templates. Professional adds custom PDF templates from a library of 500+ options and group reporting. Reports can go out by email or zip file, with password protection. Export as CSV and XLS. Professional has more than 3 dozen data exports. Participants can build development plans from their results.
features.languages: More than 100 languages, with up to 20 in one project. Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Italian use neural machine translation. Customers can supply their own translations. The Multi-language Surveys add-on costs $17 per review, and without it reviews run in English only. The languages page limits regional dialects and automatic translation of comments to the Enterprise Edition.
features.integrations: SAML 2.0 SSO as a $1,200 per year add-on. HRIS import by SFTP (JSON or CSV) or by Excel. A REST API on Professional Plus. Slack and Microsoft Teams: Not found.
features.ai: Optional. Administrators turn AI features on. Features: AI survey generation, narrative report summaries, action plans, a writing assistant for raters, comment summaries, InsightScout Q&A on results, development suggestions and automatic translation. Most sit in the paid Insights Toolkit. Accounts can choose OpenAI or Anthropic Claude. The vendor states that customer data is not used to train AI models and that InsightScout never identifies raters.

security.hosting: Microsoft Azure in the EU (West Europe), for the platform and the managed SQL database. The optional Mailgun email service is also hosted in the EU. Region choice: Not published. An older privacy page says servers are in the United States and would move to the EU from 17 April 2020. The trust centre is the more recent statement.
security.certificates: EchoSpan states no certification of its own. It says Microsoft Azure holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001. Microsoft's SOC 2 report needs a login to the Microsoft Service Trust Portal. EchoSpan runs periodic third-party penetration tests. Results are visible only to registered administrators.
security.ai_subprocessors: OpenAI (ChatGPT API, optional) and Anthropic (Claude API, listed as limited availability). Other subprocessors: Microsoft Azure, Mailgun, Stripe and Help Scout. The vendor states that data sent to OpenAI and Anthropic is not used to train publicly available models.
security.gdpr: A GDPR compliance statement and a DPA (PDF) are linked from the trust centre. Users can ask for a copy of their personal data, or for deletion, by email to privacy@echospan.com. The privacy page says data is removed within 90 days after a subscription ends. EU representative: Not found. EU AI Act documentation for each AI feature is available on request.

strengths: More than 100 languages, with Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Italian on neural machine translation.
A competency library of 80+ competencies, plus import of your own.
Anonymity controls: a minimum number of responses per rater group, and rater group pooling on Professional and above.
Hosted on Azure in West Europe, with a DPA and a list of subprocessors.
AI features are optional and are turned on by administrators.
SSO (SAML 2.0), HRIS import by SFTP, and a REST API on Professional Plus.
limitations: The vendor does not publish base prices for the 360 plans. Only add-ons carry prices.
AI tools, extra languages and SSO are paid add-ons: $44 per review, $17 per review and $1,200 per year.
Rater group pooling needs Professional, and the API needs Professional Plus.
No certification of its own. SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are held by Azure.
Without the Multi-language Surveys add-on, reviews run in English only.
fit: Organisations and consultants that need many survey languages, European hosting or optional AI tools.

name: Huckleberry

features.raters: Colleagues that the recipient asks. Rater types such as manager, peers and direct reports are not named. External raters: Not found.

Feedback received belongs to the recipient, and the privacy policy says admins cannot see 360 content unless the recipient shares it. A giver can ask by email to remove their attributed feedback. Summaries made from it may remain in aggregated form.
features.questions: The AI coach runs a strengths-based interview instead of a fixed questionnaire. A competency model is on the Team plan. Templates and custom questions: Not found.

Admins get a weekly AI brief with themes by team, department and company, and never individual content. Recipients can export their coaching profile and received feedback at any time.
features.languages: Multi-language support is listed on the Enterprise plan. No languages are named.
features.integrations: Team plan: 10+ HRIS integrations. The product pages name BambooHR, Workday, Rippling, HiBob and Gusto, plus Lattice and Culture Amp. Google Calendar and Granola are on all plans. The FAQ says Slack and Teams surface communication context. SSO and an API: Not found.
features.ai: AI is central. An AI voice coach interviews colleagues and runs coaching sessions, and the AI writes the growth plans. ElevenLabs provides real-time voice AI. Anthropic provides AI text processing. Audio is not stored. The transcript is used to write a summary and then discarded, and a short encrypted excerpt is kept so a session can resume. The vendor states that conversations are not used to train models. Whether AI can be switched off for the feedback flow: Not found.

security.hosting: The privacy policy says the service is operated from the United States. The DPA lists Supabase (database hosting, US), Vercel (web hosting, US) and AWS (key management, US). EU data residency is offered on enterprise plans only. Enterprise customers can ask for a deployment outside the US under a separate agreement.
security.certificates: SOC 2: the vendor says it has been compliant since June 2026 and that certification is expected soon. No report or certificate is published. ISO 27001: the vendor says its management system is built against the 2022 standard. It does not claim certification.
security.ai_subprocessors: ElevenLabs (real-time voice AI, US) and Anthropic (AI text processing, US). The DPA says Anthropic deletes session transcripts and uploaded documents within 30 days, or keeps them up to 2 years if flagged for a usage policy breach, and never uses them for training. Apollo.io (profile enrichment, US) is also listed.
security.gdpr: A DPA at gethuckleberry.com/dpa applies to Team and Enterprise plans and is part of the Terms with no signature needed. EEA transfers use the Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two), and UK transfers use the UK Addendum. Customers can export company data within 30 days after termination. Remaining data is deleted after 30 days, and backups may last up to 30 days. Written confirmation of deletion is available on request. EU representative: Not found.

strengths: A free plan that includes 360 feedback, with no credit card.
Colleagues give feedback by voice in about five minutes, with no form to fill in.
List prices are public in USD: $25 a month for one person and $20 per seat per month for teams.
The recipient owns the feedback received and can export it.
Voice audio is not stored, and the vendor states conversations are not used to train models.
The DPA and subprocessor list are published, with Standard Contractual Clauses for EEA transfers.
limitations: Feedback is named. Anonymous feedback is not offered.
No rater types, minimum responses or report format are documented for 360.
Data is processed in the United States. EU data residency needs an enterprise plan.
No SOC 2 report or certificate is published. The vendor says certification is expected soon.
Multi-language support is listed for Enterprise only, and SSO is not mentioned.
fit: One person or a team that wants coaching and a growth plan after named, voice-based feedback.

name: Leapsome

features.reports: Subject report with Insights (responses, comments, top relative strengths and opportunities, overall scores by rater category), Comments, and All Responses (bar chart or table).
